exposure: COVID-19 social restrictions (lockdown period, post-lockdown period)
cohort: The study participants included all live deliveries between April 1 and September 30 for the years 2021 and 2022 at the study hospitals.
finding: The COVID-19 lockdown period was associated with lower gestational diabetes mellitus, while the post-lockdown period was linked to higher birth length and hypertension in pregnancy; additionally, maternal COVID-19 infection during lockdown was associated with lower neonatal birth weight at 37-39 weeks of gestation.
mod_finding: The overall rate of cesarean delivery was not associated with the lockdown period.
cross-section timing: Data was collected for live deliveries between April 1 and September 30 for the years 2021 and 2022, categorized into pre-lockdown (April 1-Sep 30, 2021), during lockdown (April 1-May 31, 2022), and post-lockdown (June 1-Sep 30, 2022) periods.
